title: The Last Trail
premise: Oscar Dravenmoor, a railroad engineer who survives by mapping abandoned lines no one else dares to run, is hired by a desperate widow to find a vanished government survey team last seen heading into the Sable Reach. Racing a ruthless salvage fleet that claims salvage rights over human lives, Oscar discovers the team was murdered to hide evidence that the fleet's owner, Aldous Vane, sabotaged his own wreck for insurance. With six tides as her deadline, Oscar must choose between escaping with proof and saving the one survey survivor held aboard Vane's flagship. She burns her own map — her livelihood and identity — to trap Vane's fleet in the closing tide, delivering justice the law never could, though it costs her everything she built.
about_author: Vesper Dunmore is the pen name of a former merchant-marine navigator who spent a decade running coastal freight before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people whose skills keep them alive but whose consciences keep them moving.

chapters.title: The Map That Costs
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She runs a night train over a closed mountain line, dodging a toll gang, establishing her rule: never stop moving. A telegram reaches her at dawn offering impossible money from a woman named Cora Ashe. The beat: wary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Widow's Bargain
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Cora Ashe reveals her husband led the vanished survey team; the government has written them off, but salvage fleets are circling the site. She offers Oscar double her year's earnings. The beat: reluctant commitment — Oscar takes the job because stopping costs more than danger.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Studying tide tables and the survey's last coordinates, she calculates she has six tides before the wreck site floods beyond reach — same window as the salvage fleet. The beat: cold arithmetic of survival, first hint this job can't be done alone.

chapters.title: The Stowaway Boy
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Departing on her engine, she discovers a teenage stowaway, Finch, who stole aboard seeking the survey team — his father was among them. She tries to leave him at a junction; he outmaneuvers her. The beat: grudging alliance, thawing heart.

chapters.title: Ghost Station
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They follow the closed line through an abandoned station and find survey gear left in perfect order — packs, instruments, rations — but no tracks, no struggle, no bodies. The beat: creeping dread; someone wanted the team erased, not lost.

chapters.title: The Fleet on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. From a ridge they spot Vane's salvage fleet — three ships, armed, moving faster than any honest operation needs. A patrol skiff nearly catches them. The beat: the race becomes real; Oscar realizes Vane expects no witnesses.

chapters.title: What the Rails Remember
chapters.summary: Finch's POV. Following an old maintenance spur only Oscar's map knows, Finch reflects on his father's letters hinting at 'something wrong with the manifest.' They find a torn survey logbook page naming Vane's ship. The beat: hope sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Drowned Cut
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The line ends at a flooded rail cut they must cross at low tide, racing the water. They wade through with the engine's fate uncertain, reaching the survey camp's final position. The beat: visceral peril; Oscar risks her one irreplaceable asset.

chapters.title: Marks in the Clay
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the camp they find shallow graves and boot prints from Vane's crew — the survey team found evidence and were silenced. One grave is empty, its marker scratched with a live signal code. The beat: grief curdling into fury; someone survived.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Following the signal code, they find surveyor Elias Wren hiding in a sea cave, wounded. He confirms Vane scuttled his own vessel for insurance and killed the team to bury the proof. The beat: the mystery becomes a moral weight — testimony worth killing for.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Vane's men intercept them; instead of bullets, Vane himself offers Oscar a fortune and a place in his fleet — he respects her map work. She stalls. The beat: temptation articulated perfectly; power showing its seductive face.

chapters.title: Finch's Choice
chapters.summary: Finch's POV. Captured briefly aboard Vane's flagship, Finch sees the empty grave's occupant alive — a coerced witness Vane keeps as leverage. Finch escapes but must choose between fleeing and signaling Oscar. The beat: courage inherited from a dead father.

chapters.title: Two Tides
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Reunited with Finch and Wren, Oscar plans: get Wren's testimony to a federal magistrate across the Reach before the fleet silences everyone. Two tides remain. The beat: resolve hardening; the escape plan takes shape.

chapters.title: Burning the Map
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. To mislead Vane's trackers, Oscar destroys her master map — her livelihood, her legend, her safety. Finch watches her do it without flinching. The beat: sacrifice made concrete; the price of survival paid in advance.

chapters.title: The Trap Line
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Using memorized knowledge of the closed lines, Oscar lures Vane's lead pursuit ship onto a washed-out trestle, crippling it. Vane understands he's been played. The beat: triumph with teeth — she's now made a mortal enemy.

chapters.title: Storm Tide
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A storm arrives early; the final tide will be lethal. Wren, feverish, dictates his testimony while Oscar and Finch fight to keep him alive and moving. The beat: fragility of truth — justice depends on one failing body.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Door
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They reach the magistrate's outpost hours ahead of Vane's lawyers — but the magistrate is on Vane's payroll and refuses the testimony. The beat: crushing betrayal; the law itself is bought, and justice outside the law becomes the only road.

chapters.title: One Tide Left
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Cornered, Oscar improvises: broadcast Wren's testimony and the evidence ledger over the fleet's own emergency channel, forcing every port authority in the region to hear it. The beat: audacious reversal; turning Vane's machinery against him.

chapters.title: The Closing Water
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Vane corners them at the drowned cut as the final tide closes. Oscar offers him the choice she promised: testify or drown with his fleet trapped by her rerouted line. He chooses the water; his crew does not follow him down. The beat: climax — power drowning in its own corruption.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Finch's POV. In the aftermath, independent magistrates arrive to the broadcast's fallout. Wren testifies; Vane, pulled half-drowned from the cut, faces trial. Cora Ashe gets her answer about her husband. The beat: bittersweet vindication; the law arrives late but arrives.

chapters.title: What Remains of the Map
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Offered a government post and a rebuilt reputation, Oscar declines — she redraws her map from memory, minus the lines she'd rather keep closed. Finch asks to stay on as her apprentice. The beat: quiet healing; family chosen, not found.

chapters.title: The Last Trail
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Epilogue. Months later, a new telegram arrives with another impossible offer. Oscar reads it by firelight, glances at Finch asleep under the engine, and smiles — then starts planning the route. The beat: the road goes on; some people are made for the moving.
